<term>Yi Yu</term> said: I have frequently visited the altar site to inspect the work. The completion date is still far off. The labor is extremely massive. From the beginning, the <term>Seogyok Dogam</term> <gloss>Directorate for Stone Work</gloss> was supervised only by the ministers of the Ministry of Rites and Ministry of Works for the sake of simplicity. However, those two ministers each have multiple concurrent roles, such as attending the Royal Lectures or sitting at the <term>Geum-o</term> <gloss>State Tribunal</gloss>. They cannot focus solely on the altar work. Sometimes the office is empty, and only one person is watching the work, which is truly worrying. Although it is difficult to suddenly establish a full <term>Dogam</term> <gloss>Directorate</gloss>, this project is different from others. It would be good to let other officials take over their concurrent duties so they can focus entirely on supervising the altar work. 

<term>Min Jin-hu</term> said: Initially, I was supervising along with <term>Seo Jong-tae</term> and <term>Kim Jin-gyu</term>. Unexpectedly, <term>Jin-gyu</term> was transferred, and I have been handling it alone without a moment’s rest. Now that the Vice Minister of Rites has been appointed, how about ordering him to supervise together? 

<term>Yi Yu</term> said: Regarding <term>Jin-gyu</term>, because the Minister was away, he was made to watch the work. However, because of a single word of mine, he felt aggrieved and did not come out, and then he was transferred. Now there is no need to make the Vice Minister supervise the labor together. It would be appropriate to simply excuse the two ministers from their other duties so they can focus on supervising. 

The King said: Do as suggested. 

<term>Yi Yu</term> said: Directorates are usually staffed by the Ministries of Taxation, Rites, and Works. This altar labor was decided in haste without establishing a formal name.

O <term>Mṛttikā</term>! O <term>Aśvakrāntā</term>! O you who are trodden by the horse, the all-pervading Supreme Self! O <term>Rathakrāntā</term>! 33. O <term>Mṛttikā</term>! Destroy my sin.

<margin>See various old watchtowers along the beach.</margin>
Furthermore, one sees here along the beach various very old towers, and among others two special ones that have been renewed, in which the Druze keep watch in order to quickly discover pirates. But the others, of which there are still many standing along the beach, each a mile apart, have mostly fallen into decay due to age.

Some believe that they were built in the past by order of the Roman Emperors so that, if any people rebelled or a war arose suddenly, one would have news of it sooner in Constantinople. They gave the signal and sign by night with a bright flame of fire, and by day with heavy smoke, before the invention of the cannon; although even now, these signs are maintained here in place of cannon shots.

In the afternoon, when the wind had died down and our progress was therefore slow, we saw the small village of Carniola high up in the evening; and not long after that, below at the end of the high Lebanon mountains toward the south, the city of Sidon, still called <term>Seida</term> <gloss>local name for Sidon</gloss> by the inhabitants at this time. It is not particularly large, but in outward appearance, it is fairly well built and guarded by two castles, of which one lies on a high cliff toward the north and the other on a high hill. <margin>BOOK II.</margin> This is the form of the sneezing funnel <note>original: "infundibulum sternutatorium"</note> with which oils or medicines are dripped into the nose. <margin>SECTION XXIV.</margin>

<note>An engraving of a nasal funnel (infundibulum) with the Arabic word "mas'ut" (nasal dropper) written inside the central bulb.</note>

It should be made of silver or copper, similar to a small lamp, like an oil vessel, open, and its canal constructed in the same manner. And if you wish, you may make the tube closed, like a reed, and the oil chamber of the sneezing funnel is made expanded and open. It has a handle, as you see, by which you hold it when you instill oil, or whatever you wish of juices, or liquid things.

SECTION TWENTY-FIFTH. On Papules and Warts Arising on the Tip of the Nose. <margin>SECTION XXV.</margin>

**V**ery often, papules and warts arise on the tip of the nose, which grow and increase daily until their appearance becomes deformed. It is therefore necessary that when they first appear, you excise and eradicate them entirely, and apply to the area cautery, either with fire or a burning medicine that serves the purpose of a cautery. But if the excision is delayed until they become large, consider the matter; if the wart is calcified, hard, dull in color, and has little sensation, do not treat it with iron <note>the scalpel</note>, for it is a cancerous tumor. I have very often seen great calamities arise from the excision of these tumors for those who were afflicted by them. But if the tumor is soft to the touch, not dull in color, and you see that it can be cut out entirely, then purge the patient, and excise it without fear, and treat the area with drying and styptic agents until it is healed, if God wills it.

<summary>This page describes a nasal funnel for medication and the surgical management of nasal warts, emphasizing the avoidance of surgery for likely cancerous growths.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the technical specifications for identification flags within the military hierarchy. Having previously discussed the banners of high-ranking generals and company commanders, the text now details the equipment for the Squad Leader (duìzhǎng), the most basic level of command in the Ming military structure.</meta>

# Treatise on Armament Technology, Volume 101

### Military Equipment: Warfare — Banners and Flags, Part 3

The **Squad Leader’s identifying flag** is one square foot in size. The pole used for this flag is a **long spear**, fifteen feet in length. The flag itself is to be suspended at a height of nine feet from the ground.
<note>original: 隊長認旗方一尺桿用長鎗一丈五尺旗懸高九尺. In the Ming military system popularized by General Qi Jiguang, the "long spear" served as both a primary weapon and a mobile flagpole, ensuring the squad leader could lead the charge while remaining a visible point of alignment for his twelve men.</note>

The total weight is two catties.
<note>original: 重二斤 (zhòng èr jīn). A "catty" or jin during the Ming period was approximately 590 grams, making the entire assembly roughly 1.2 kilograms or 2.6 pounds.</note>

<term>Squad Leader<note>original: 隊長 (duìzhǎng). The leader of a *duì*, the smallest tactical unit. In the "Mandarin Duck Formation," this leader stood at the front, directing the combined efforts of spearmen, shield-bearers, and branch-wielders.</note></term>

<term>Identifying Flag<note>original: 認旗 (rènqí). Also known as "recognition flags," these allowed soldiers to identify their specific unit and leader amidst the smoke and chaos of the battlefield.</note></term>

<term>Measurements (Zhang and Chi)<note>original: 丈 (zhàng) and 尺 (chǐ). One *zhàng* contains ten *chǐ*. In the 16th century, 15 *chǐ* (one *zhàng* five *chǐ*) would be roughly 4.8 meters or 15.7 feet.</note></term>

<summary>This passage defines the physical dimensions and weight of a Squad Leader's identification flag, noting its attachment to a functional long spear for visibility and utility.</summary>

Because the minerals here are such coagulated, dried <unclear>bodies</unclear>, they also require another <term>penetrans</term> <gloss>penetrating agent</gloss> like animals and vegetables. Therefore, we take the specific universal seed as the <term>Spiritum Dei</term> <gloss>Spirit of God</gloss> and Antimony, and because it misuses the Sun, it equips the Sun or helps it to arrive.

Otherwise, the spirit of the Sun and Gold is to be made at all times in quantity, which is a <term>proprium humidum mineralium</term> <gloss>specific moisture of minerals</gloss> for all ripeness and wise <term>astris</term> <gloss>stars or essences</gloss>.

# Monthly Solitude and Void Positions
<note>In traditional Chinese metaphysics and military theory, "Solitude" (Gu) and "Void" (Xu) are paired opposites used to determine favorable directions. "Solitude" represents a concentrated, singular force of energy, while "Void" represents emptiness or vulnerability. A common strategic maxim was to "occupy the Solitude and strike the Void."</note>

| Month | Location of Solitude | Location of the Void |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Second Month | Solitude is at **Gen**, in the Northeast <term>Gen (艮): The trigram representing the Mountain and the Northeast direction.</term> | Void is in the Southwest |
| Third Month | Solitude is at **Zhen**, in the True East <term>Zhen (震): The trigram representing Thunder and the East direction.</term> | Void is in the True West |
| Fourth Month | Solitude is at **Xun**, in the Southeast <term>Xun (巽): The trigram representing Wind and the Southeast direction.</term> | Void is in the Northwest |
| Fifth Month | Solitude is at **Xun**, in the Southeast | Void is in the Northwest |
| Sixth Month | Solitude is at **Li**, in the True South <term>Li (離): The trigram representing Fire and the South direction.</term> | Void is in the True North |
| Seventh Month | Solitude is at **Kun**, in the Southwest <term>Kun (坤): The trigram representing the Earth and the Southwest direction.</term> | Void is in the Northeast |
| Eighth Month | Solitude is at **Kun**, in the Southwest | Void is in the Northeast |
| Ninth Month | Solitude is at **Dui**, in the True West <term>Dui (兌): The trigram representing the Lake and the West direction.</term> | Void is in the True East |
| Tenth Month | Solitude is at **Qian**, in the Northwest <term>Qian (乾): The trigram representing Heaven and the Northwest direction.</term> | Void is in the Southeast |

<note>Notice that the positions of Solitude and Void are always direct opposites on the compass. For example, in the Second Month, Solitude is Northeast while the Void is Southwest. Some months, such as the Fourth and Fifth, or the Seventh and Eighth, share the same directional alignments.</note>

<header>Musa Dezima.</header>
<sig>Y</sig>

vayan con Dios, que ya esto se ha acabado:
que quedandome sola, y retirada,
mi borrador harè mas descansada.
Por el cabello empieço, estense quedos,
que ay aqui que pintar muchos enredos;
no hallo comparacion que bien les quadre:
que para poco me pariò mi madre!
Rayos del Sol? ya aquello se ha passado,
la Pregmatica nueva lo ha quitado.
Cuerda de arco de amor, en dulce trance?
esso es llamarlo Cerda, en buen Romance.
Que linda ocasion era:
de tomar la ocasion por la molleras;
pero aquessa ocasion yà se ha passado,
y calva està, de averla repelado.
Y assi, en su calva lisa,
su cabellera irà tambien postiza:
y el que llega à cogella,
se queda con el pelo, y no con ella;
y en fin despues de tanto dar en ellos,
que tenemos, mi Musa, de cabello?
el de Absalon viniera aqui nacido,
por tener mi discurso suspendido:
mas no quiero meterme yo en honduras,
ni en hazerme que entiendo de Escritura.
En ser cabello de Lifarda quede,
que es lo que encarecerse mas se puede,
y baxese à la frente mi reparo,
gracias à Dios, que salgo azia lo claro,
que me pude perder en su espesura,
si no saliera por la comissura.
Tendrà, pues, la tal frente,
vna cavalleria largamente,
segun està de limpia, y despejada.

<header>Tenth Muse.</header>
<sig>Y</sig>

go with God, for this is already finished:
for staying alone, and withdrawn,
my draft will be more rested.
I begin with the hair, keep still,
for there is much entanglement here to paint;
I find no comparison that fits them well:
for little indeed did my mother give birth to me!
Rays of the Sun? that has already passed,
the new <term>Pragmática</term> <gloss>royal edict/sumptuary law</gloss> has removed it.
Bowstring of love, in a sweet trance?
that is to call it "Bristle," in good Spanish.
What a lovely occasion it was:
to take the opportunity by the forelock;
but that opportunity has already passed,
and it is bald, from having been plucked.
And so, on its smooth baldness,
its wig will also be artificial:
and whoever arrives to catch it,
is left with the hair, and not with her;
and in the end after so much banging on them,
what do we have, my Muse, of hair?
that of <note>Absalom, the biblical figure known for his long hair</note> could have been born here,
for having my discourse suspended:
but I do not want to get myself into deep waters,
nor make myself out to understand Scripture.
Let it remain as Lifarda's hair,
which is the most that can be praised,
and let my observation descend to the forehead,
thanks to God, I am heading toward the clear,
for I could have lost myself in its thickness,
if I had not come out through the gap.
The said forehead will have,
a large amount of cavalry,
as it is clean and clear.

# Anangaranga [Seventh Section]

The man should touch his own <term>linga</term> <gloss>phallus</gloss> with the <term>Tagara</term> plant and touch her left foot. This makes her subject to him in all things, without a doubt. (21)
When <term>Sindura</term> <gloss>red lead/vermilion</gloss> and <term>Madhuka</term> <gloss>Bassia latifolia</gloss> are mixed in equal parts with honey, the woman who worships the <term>linga</term> of the world <note>referring to the partner's phallus</note> will become completely compliant. (22)
Take the phallus of a bear, mix it with honey, and apply it to the male organ twice. She who is approached by this will become controlled. (23)
Mix <term>Vacha</term> <gloss>Acorus calamus</gloss>, gold, <term>Shambhubeja</term>, camphor, and sandalwood. When one who has anointed his <term>linga</term> with this approaches a woman, she becomes controlled. (24)

### Incense
Grind sandalwood, saffron, <term>Vyadhi</term> <gloss>kantakari/wild eggplant</gloss>, <term>Kalanga</term>, flowers, water, and <term>Devadaru</term> <gloss>Himalayan cedar</gloss>, and mix them with honey. (25)
This incense, known as <term>Chintamani</term>, is supreme for fascination. When applied according to the method, it brings all tasks to fruition. (26)
Mix <term>Ela</term> <gloss>cardamom</term>, <term>Sarjerasa</term> <gloss>resin</gloss>, <term>Tarkshya</term> <gloss>Shala tree</gloss>, sandalwood, young <term>Vacha</term>, and <term>Shringi</term> <gloss>medicinal herb</gloss> in equal parts. This incense will fascinate the entire world. (27)

<note>1. Vyadhi: commonly known as "Kuta." The Lahore edition reads "Vyaghri, Kushmanda flower, and water." This reading seems correct. Vyaghri is Kantakarika.
2. Ela: Cardamom.
3. Sarjerasa: Known as "Rala" (resin).
4. Tarkshya: Shala tree.
5. Yuvati: Known as "Kakoli" or Priyangu.
6. Shringi: A powerful medicinal herb.</note>

Quæ igitur ut distincta ac terminata appareat oportet radios qui ab uno Solis puncto procedunt, hoc est, qui paralleli inter se deferuntur in lentem AB, in uno rursus tabulæ puncto colligi. Quapropter paulo major debet esse distantia lentium AB & D quam in constitutione telescopii media, sive quæ bene videnti fuerit accommodata; ac talis requiritur positio lentis D, ut in continua sint proportione EK, ED, EH.

The other lens at D is concave or convex, for either form of the telescope is suitable for this purpose, and indeed that which is of two convexes is more so, since it exhibits erect pictures, whereas the other inverts them. The point K of lens D becomes the meeting point or the dispersal point of the parallel rays coming from the side where H is, and a white board is set at H to receive the Sun's image. Therefore, so that it may appear distinct and well-defined, it is necessary that the rays which proceed from one point of the Sun, that is, which are carried parallel to each other into lens AB, be gathered again at one point on the board. For this reason, the distance between lenses AB and D must be slightly greater than in the median construction of the telescope, or that which was accommodated for one seeing well; and such a position of lens D is required that EK, ED, and EH are in continued proportion.

->LION AND LITTLE JACKAL<-

At another time there was a meeting of the animals, and Lion was the chief at the meeting. Little Jackal wanted to attend, but there was a law made that no one should be present unless he had horns. So Little Jackal took wax out of a nest of bees, and made horns for himself with it. He fastened the horns on his head, and went to the meeting. Lion did not know him on account of the horns. But he sat near the fire and went to sleep, when the horns melted.

Lion looked at him and saw who it was. He immediately tried to catch him, but Little Jackal was quick in springing away. He ran under an overhanging rock and sang out: "Help! help! this rock is falling upon me!"

Lion went for a pole to prop up the rock that he might get at Little Jackal. While he was away, Little Jackal escaped.

After that they became companions again, and went hunting another time. They killed an ox. Lion said: "I will watch it while you carry the pieces away."

Lion gave him the breast, and said: "Take this to my wife."

The Lion looked at him and saw who it was. He immediately tried to catch him, but Little Jackal was quick in springing away. He ran under an overhanging rock and sang out, "Help! help! This rock is falling upon me!"

The Lion went for a pole to prop up the rock so that he might get at Little Jackal. While he was away, Little Jackal escaped.

After that, they became companions again and went hunting another time. They killed an ox. The Lion said, "I will watch it while you carry the pieces away."

Venant donq S. M. a Blois au mois de May, on conſeilloit a M. du Pleſſis apres une telle indignation de ſe reculer plus loin. Ce qu'il ne voulut, aſſeuré de ſon innocence & ſe remettant en tout a la providence de Dieu. Et de faict S. M. dit a M. de Villeroy que s'il le venoit trouver il luy feroit bon viſage; Meſmes a M. de Lomenie qu'il vouloit qu'il deſcendiſt juſques a Saumur pour le voir de ſa part. Mais M. de Roſni, ſoit qu'il vouluſt avoir l'obligation de l'avoir remis avec le Roy, ſoit que du tout il vouluſt deſtourner ce coup, dit a S. M. qu'au premier jour il iroit voir luy meſme avec ſa femme niepce de M. du Pleſſis, & qu'il luy devoit ceſt office. Ce que depuis il excuſa par la precipitation du retour; Et ainſi M. du Pleſſis ne vid ny l'un ny l'autre; Selon ſon ſouhait a la verité; parce qu'eſtant reſolu de publier ſa Reſponſe a l'Eveſque d'Eureux lors toute preſte, il craignoit, que pour prix de rentrer en la bonne grace de S. M. on ne luy impoſaſt condition de n'eſcrire plus. Et cela ne pouvoit il accepter en bonne conſcience, ny refuſer ſans offenſer le Roy. Mais S. M. ayant tourné ſon chemin vers Paris, pour effacer ſa faute, ſi on y en trouvoit, il luy envoye le Sieur Marbaut ſon Secretaire avec lettres du 2. Iuin en ces motz.

> *SIRE, le dernier viſage que j'eus ce malheur de recevoir de V. M. ma fait apprehender de me preſenter devant vous, n'eſtant aſſés aſſeuré de voſtre bonne grace. Non toutefois que ie n'aye entreveu en mes tenebres quelques eſtincelles de voſtre bonté envers moy; mais ſi toſt eſteintes, quelles m'ont deu esblouir pluſtoſt que m'eſclairer; Si peu ſuivies que jai deu pluſtoſt me retenir en une douteuſe reverence, que me laiſſer aller a une confiance preſomptueuſe. ### THE LIFE OF MONSIEUR DU PLESSIS

From that moment, the King even began to soften his stance toward Monsieur du Plessis and recommended that he be better treated in his private affairs. This was perhaps due to the shock of such an atrocious proceeding <note>referring to the assassination plot</note>, or perhaps because of the distress he felt over the Conspiracy of Marshal de Biron, which he was discovering day by day, and against which he judged that Du Plessis's service could be useful to him. Thus, when His Majesty came to Blois in the month of May, Monsieur du Plessis was advised, after such a display of royal indignation, to withdraw further away. This he would not do, being assured of his innocence and committing himself entirely to the providence of God. And indeed, His Majesty told Monsieur de Villeroy that if Du Plessis came to find him, he would receive him warmly; he even told Monsieur de Loménie <note>Antoine de Loménie, another of the King's secretaries of state.</note> that he wanted him to travel down to Saumur to see Du Plessis on his behalf. 

But Monsieur de Rosny <note>Maximilien de Béthune, Duke of Sully, a powerful minister and Du Plessis's nephew by marriage.</note>—whether he wished to have the credit for reconciling him with the King, or whether he wished to avert this meeting entirely—told His Majesty that at the first opportunity he would go see him himself with his wife, the niece of Monsieur du Plessis, and that he owed him this service. He later excused this by the haste of his return; and thus Monsieur du Plessis saw neither the one nor the other. This was, in truth, according to his own wish; because, being resolved to publish his *Response to the Bishop of Évreux* <note>Jacques Davy du Perron, the Bishop of Évreux, who had "defeated" Du Plessis in the famous 1600 Fontainebleau debate regarding alleged false citations in Du Plessis's book on the Eucharist.</note> which was then ready, he feared that as a price for returning to His Majesty’s good graces, they might impose a condition that he write no more. This he could not accept in good conscience, nor could he refuse it without offending the King. But His Majesty having turned his path toward Paris, Monsieur du Plessis sent Monsieur Marbaut, his secretary, to erase his fault—if any were found—with letters dated June 2nd in these words:

> *SIRE, the last look I had the misfortune of receiving from Your Majesty has made me apprehensive about presenting myself before you, not being sufficiently assured of your good graces. Not, however, that I have not glimpsed through my darkness some sparks of your goodness toward me; but they were so quickly extinguished that they served to dazzle rather than enlighten me; so little followed by action that I felt I must restrain myself in a doubtful reverence, rather than allow myself a presumptuous confidence. I therefore have recourse, SIRE, to most humbly beseeching Your Majesty to forgive me either for this justified fear or this hesitant respect; and nevertheless to remember the fidelity of my years passed,*

Du Plessis remains cautious, choosing to prioritize the publication of his theological defense against the Bishop of Évreux over immediate political reconciliation.</summary>
